description: 64 red LEDs in an 8×8 grid behind 16 pins: each row's LEDs share an anode pin (R1–R8) and each column's LEDs share a cathode pin (C1–C8).
how_to_use: An LED lights when its row pin is HIGH and its column pin is LOW. Drive all 16 pins from the Arduino (column pins through 220 Ω resistors) and scan the rows fast enough that the eye sees a steady picture (row-column scanning).

pins.R1: row 1: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R2: row 2: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R3: row 3: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R4: row 4: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R5: row 5: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R6: row 6: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R7: row 7: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.R8: row 8: the anodes (+) of the 8 LEDs in that row
pins.C1: column 1: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C2: column 2: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C3: column 3: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C4: column 4: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C5: column 5: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C6: column 6: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C7: column 7: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column
pins.C8: column 8: the cathodes (−) of the 8 LEDs in that column

plain.what: 64 little red lights in an 8×8 grid — draw dots, letters and pictures.
plain.how: 8 row pins (+) and 8 column pins (−). A dot lights where its row is HIGH and its column is LOW; the Arduino flicks through the rows so fast it looks steady.
